A measurement of blood pressure is expressed using the reading 
for systolic pressure as the ﬁ rst (higher) number and the read-
ing for diastolic pressure as the second (lower) number. A reading
greater than or equal to 140/90 mmHg is considered to be hyper-
tensive. However, it is not necessary for both systolic and diastolic 
blood pressure to be elevated for an individual to be considered 
hypertensive; thus, readings of 140/80 mmHg or 120/90 mmHg
